content.content:
1	# A theme for your app
2	
3	This page is for an app that links the RipulAgent package and wants its own
4	fonts and colours to come from a theme: one JSON document, light and dark,
5	switchable while the app runs. It starts from "add the package" and is in the
6	order to do the work. The full contract, with every measurement behind a rule
7	here, is [theming.md](theming.md); you should not need it to get through this
8	page.
9	
10	What you write, in total: one line at the root, a theme document, your font
11	files, one line of build setup for the View Explorer, and whatever the
12	migration command leaves for a person to decide. Everything else is the SDK's.
13	
14	Where a thing is not built, this page says so. The list is at the end.
15	
16	**If an agent is doing the work,** give it the procedure first: what to measure
17	before the first edit, which level to start at, where to stop and ask, and how
18	to prove nothing moved. It is a skill file in this package,
19	`tools/skills/theme-an-app/SKILL.md`, and one command copies it to where a
20	coding agent in your repository finds it (`.claude/skills` for Claude Code,
21	`.agents/skills` for Codex):
22	
23	```bash
24	<the package checkout>/tools/ripul-theme install-skill <your repository>
25	```
26	
27	An agent running inside Ripul reads the same text as the `theming` guide of its
28	`ripul_guide` tool. This page is the reference that procedure points to.
29	
30	## The idea
31	
32	Every token has a default that is the system value you write today.
33	`Font.ripul(.body)` is `Font.body`. `.ripul(.textSecondary)` is the system's
34	`.secondary` style. So moving a call site to a token changes no pixel, and an
35	app with no theme document looks exactly as it did. A document changes a token
36	only by naming it.
37	
38	## With no change to your source
39	
40	There are two ways to adopt the theme. The numbered steps below are the first:
41	you move your call sites to tokens, with a command that does most of it. This
42	section is the second: you change settings and add files, and no line of your
43	Swift changes. It is in the package from release 0.7.172, and it has been
44	measured on one app. It is where to start: the numbered steps are for an app
45	that wants what this does not reach.
46	
47	What you do:
48	
49	1. Add the package to the app target, as in step 1 below, without the root
50	   line.
51	2. Put your theme document and font files in the bundle (steps 2 and 3).
52	3. Switch on the package's build-tool plug-in, `RipulThemeRedirect`, for the app
53	   target: in Xcode, the target's Build Phases, "Run Build Tool Plug-ins", add
54	   it. In an XcodeGen `project.yml`:
55	
56	   ```yaml
57	       buildToolPlugins:
58	         - plugin: RipulThemeRedirect
59	           package: RipulAgent
60	   ```
61	4. Allow the plug-in to run. Xcode asks once, "Trust & Enable". A command-line
62	   build passes `-skipPackagePluginValidation` to `xcodebuild`; without it the
63	   build fails with the one line `Validate plug-in “RipulThemeRedirect” in
64	   package “ripul-ios-sdk”` (measured with the package fetched by version; a
65	   package added by local path needs neither). Add the flag to your build
66	   scripts too.
67	
68	With one theme document in the bundle, that document is the app's theme. With
69	several, name one with the Info.plist key `RipulTheme`.
70	
71	**How it works.** On every build the plug-in writes one Swift file into the
72	build folder, and Xcode compiles it into your app's own module. The file
73	declares SwiftUI's names again: `Font.body` and the other text styles,
74	`Font.system(size:)`, `Color.red`, `Color(.systemBackground)`,
75	`.foregroundStyle(.secondary)`, `WindowGroup`. Inside your module your
76	declaration of a name is chosen over SwiftUI's, so your existing `.font(.body)`
77	calls the generated one, which is one call into the SDK. With no theme each
78	returns exactly what SwiftUI's would have. Nothing is added to your repository.
79	
80	**What it reaches,** with no edit:
81	
82	| You wrote | It follows |
83	|---|---|
84	| `.font(.body)`, `.font(.caption.weight(.semibold))`, `Font.body` | the type role of that name |
85	| `.font(.system(size: 14, weight: .medium))` | the text family at that size |
86	| `.system(.title, design: .serif)`, `.system(size: 22, design: .serif)`, and your own helper built on them | the display family, once a theme names one; the system's serif until then, with no second document |
87	| `design: .monospaced` | the code family |
88	| a font on an `Image` | nothing: a symbol keeps its system size |
89	| `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` and the other hierarchy styles | the text roles |
90	| `Color(.systemBackground)`, `Color(.systemGroupedBackground)`, `Color(.secondarySystemGroupedBackground)` | `canvas`, `surfaceSunken`, `surface` |
91	| `Color.red`, `.foregroundStyle(.orange)`, green, blue, gray | `danger`, `warning`, `success`, `info`, `neutral` |
92	| `WindowGroup { … }` | the theme root, with no line written: the accent, the body font for text with none, navigation titles, tab bar labels |
93	| identified elements | the View Explorer names their tokens (Debug builds), with no build phase |
94	
95	**What it does not reach.** These stay the system's under a theme, where the
96	migration command or a line of yours would have reached them:
97	
98	- text with no colour of its own, as in "What it leaves for you", 1;
99	- lists, section headers and empty states, as in 2 and 3;
100	- a prominent button's label (`onAccent`);
101	- a hierarchy style given to `fill`, `stroke` or `background`, and one passed
102	  through a variable of a generic type;
103	- a colour of your own (`Color("BrandNavy")`), and white and black;
104	- UIKit code (`UIFont.preferredFont`, `UIColor.label`);
105	- a `Label`'s icon, which takes its size from the label's font as before.
106	
107	**What can go wrong.**
108	
109	- A name you already declare (`extension Font { static var caption }`, a type
110	  called `WindowGroup`) is left out of the generated file and yours is used.
111	  The generator reads text, not types; one it misses is a compile error naming
112	  both places.
113	- A target is redirected only if the plug-in is on for it. A framework of your
114	  own needs it switched on too.
115	- `WindowGroup(for:)` and a UIKit app delegate are not covered: put
116	  `.ripulThemeRoot()` on the root yourself and add `RIPUL_THEME_NO_ROOT` to the
117	  target's Swift compilation conditions. `RIPUL_THEME_NO_STYLES` leaves
118	  `foregroundStyle` alone.
119	- A font or colour kept in a `static let` is read once and does not follow a
120	  switch while the app runs.
121	- The rule this rests on, that a module's own declaration is preferred to an
122	  imported one of the same name and type, is how the Swift compiler behaves
123	  (measured with Swift 6.4, Xcode 27.1, in Swift 5 and Swift 6 language
124	  modes). The language's documentation does not promise it.
125	
126	The two ways mix: a file you have migrated calls the accessors directly, and
127	the rest goes through the generated file.
128	
129	## 1. Add the package and name your theme
130	
131	Pin the package (`https://github.com/ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk`), then put one
132	modifier on the root view of each window group:
133	
134	```swift
135	import RipulAgent
136	
137	WindowGroup {
138	    ContentView()
139	        .ripulThemeRoot(theme: "brand")     // brand.json in the app's bundle
140	}
141	```
142	
143	That line is the whole setup. From it the SDK:
144	
145	- finds `brand.json` in the bundle (at its top level, or in a folder named
146	  `Themes` or `Theme`), reads it and puts it in use before the first view is
147	  drawn;
148	- registers the font files the document names (step 3);
149	- keeps a choice made with `RipulTheme.select` between launches (step 6);
150	- falls back to `brand`, and then to the system look, when a document is
151	  missing, is not a theme document, or was written for a newer SDK. It logs
152	  which, with the prefix `[RipulTheme]`.
153	
154	Two other ways to say the same thing, for an app that cannot put it on a root:
155	
156	- the Info.plist key `RipulTheme` with the document's name, and a plain
157	  `.ripulThemeRoot()`;
158	- `RipulTheme.install(theme: "brand")` in the `App`'s `init` or the app
159	  delegate, for a UIKit app.
160	
161	With no name at all, `.ripulThemeRoot()` leaves the app on the system look.
162	
163	The root carries the accent (as the window's tint, so `.tint`,
164	`Color.accentColor` and control tints follow with no edit) and the theme's
165	body font for text with no font of its own. A sheet presented with
166	`.ripulSheet` has a root already. A presented `UIHostingController` of your
167	own needs `.ripulThemeRoot()` on its root view.
168	
169	## 2. Write the document
170	
171	Every key is optional, and an absent key is today's look. Start with
172	`{ "schema": 1, "name": "Brand" }`, which changes nothing, and add to it.
173	
174	```json
175	{
176	  "schema": 1,
177	  "name": "Brand",
178	  "palette": {
179	    "navy":  { "light": "#24386b", "dark": "#a9bdeb" },
180	    "paper": { "light": "#f7f3ec", "dark": "#0d1428" },
181	    "ink":   "#1c2540"
182	  },
183	  "roles": {
184	    "ripul.accent": "navy",
185	    "ripul.canvas": "paper",
186	    "ripul.text": "ink"
187	  },
188	  "typography": {
189	    "families": { "text": "Source Sans 3", "display": "Playfair Display", "code": "system-monospaced" },
190	    "roles": {
191	      "display": { "size": 34, "weight": "bold" },
192	      "eyebrow": { "tracking": 1.8, "uppercase": true }
193	    }
194	  }
195	}
196	```
197	
198	- **`palette`** names your colours. A value is `#RRGGBB`, `#RRGGBBAA`,
199	  `system:<name>` (a live system colour such as `system:label`), or a light
200	  and dark pair of those. Light and dark are written here and nowhere else.
201	- **`roles`** gives each colour role a palette name, another role, or a colour
202	  string. The fifteen roles, each with the system colour it is by default:
203	
204	  | Role | Default | For |
205	  |---|---|---|
206	  | `accent` | the app's tint | selection, links, primary buttons |
207	  | `onAccent` | white | text and icons on an accent fill |
208	  | `canvas` | `systemBackground` | the app's background |
209	  | `surface` | `secondarySystemGroupedBackground` | cards and grouped rows |
210	  | `surfaceSunken` | `systemGroupedBackground` | the ground behind cards |
211	  | `text`, `textSecondary`, `textTertiary`, `textQuaternary` | `.primary` to `.quaternary` | text |
212	  | `separator` | `separator` | hairlines |
213	  | `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `neutral` | green, orange, red, blue, grey | state |
214	
215	  The set is closed: a document cannot add a role (see the end).
216	- **`typography.families`** names the three families, `text`, `display` and
217	  `code`. Each is a font family you bundle, or one of `system`,
218	  `system-serif`, `system-rounded`, `system-monospaced`.
219	- **`typography.roles`** changes a type role: `size`, `weight`, `family`,
220	  `relativeTo`, `tracking`, `uppercase`, `catalystSize`. The roles are the
221	  eleven system text styles by their own names, plus `display` (a title in
222	  the display family), `eyebrow` and `code`.
223	
224	**A serif that is yours already.** `"display": "system-serif"` draws what
225	`.font(.system(.title, design: .serif))` draws (compared pixel for pixel in a
226	host's trial on iOS 27, at the default text size). There is no accessor for
227	`design: .serif` itself. So an app whose headings are serif today keeps them
228	by naming `system-serif` as its display family and writing
229	`.font(.ripul(.title, family: .display))` at those headings. Its document is
230	then not empty, and the plain system look (`RipulTheme.systemThemeName`) is
231	not the look it had.
232	
233	Check a dark value against its background yourself: nothing checks contrast.
234	
235	## 3. Fonts
236	
237	Put the font files in the app's bundle, at its top level or in a folder named
238	`Fonts`. Do nothing else. When a document names a family that is not the
239	system's, the SDK reads the bundled `.ttf`, `.otf` and `.ttc` files and
240	registers those that hold a face of that family. No `UIAppFonts` entry and no
241	registration call.
242	
243	- The name in the document is the font's family name ("Source Sans 3"), not
244	  its file name.
245	- A variable font takes weights; a family with one weight draws that weight
246	  whatever is asked, and the system does not fake a bold.
247	- Ship each font's licence beside it. That is yours to get right.
248	
249	## 4. Move the call sites: one command
250	
251	The package brings its tools. In an Xcode project they are in the package
252	checkout, under the build's DerivedData:
253	
254	```bash
255	# with -derivedDataPath build
256	RIPUL_THEME=build/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme
257	# with Xcode's default DerivedData
258	RIPUL_THEME=$(ls -d ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/<Project>-*/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme | head -1)
259	# in a Swift package
260	RIPUL_THEME=.build/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme
261	```
262	
263	They need `python3` and nothing else.
264	
265	```bash
266	$RIPUL_THEME migrate --dry-run --named <your source folder>   # what would change
267	$RIPUL_THEME migrate --named <your source folder>             # change it
268	```
269	
270	Every rewrite is to the token whose default is the value it replaces, so
271	nothing moves on screen. It adds no import: each file it rewrote needs
272	`import RipulAgent`, or the app one `@_exported import RipulAgent`. It rewrites:
273	
274	| You wrote | It writes |
275	|---|---|
276	| `.font(.body)`, `.font(.caption.weight(.semibold))` | `.font(.ripul(.body))`, `.font(.ripul(.caption, weight: .semibold))` |
277	| `.font(.title2)` or `.font(.system(size: 18))` on an `Image` | `.font(.ripulIcon(.title2))`, `.font(.ripulIcon(size: 18))`: a symbol's size, never themed |
278	| `.font(.system(size: 14, weight: .medium))` on a `Text` | `.font(.ripul(size: 14, weight: .medium))` |
279	| `.caption.monospaced()`, `design: .monospaced` | `family: .code` |
280	| `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` and the other hierarchy styles | `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))` |
281	| `Color.primary`, `Color.secondary` | `Color.ripul(.text)`, `Color.ripul(.textSecondary)` |
282	| `Color(.systemBackground)`, `UIColor.systemBackground`, `UIColor.label` | `Color.ripul(.canvas)`, `UIColor.ripul(.canvas)`, `UIColor.ripul(.text)` |
283	| any other system colour, `Color(.systemGray5)` | the system form, `Color.ripul(system: .systemGray5)`: drawn as before, never themed |
284	| `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)` | `.ripulProminentButtonStyle()`: its label is drawn in `onAccent` under a theme |
285	| `.buttonStyle(.glassProminent)` | `.ripulGlassProminentButtonStyle()`, likewise |
286	| with `--named`: `Color.red`, `.foregroundStyle(.orange)` | `Color.ripul(.danger)`, `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.warning))` |
287	| with `--named`: `.white`, `.black`, `.yellow` and the other hues | the system form, `.ripul(system: .white)` |
288	
289	Then see what is left, and check the change:
290	
291	```bash
292	$RIPUL_THEME check <your source folder>     # every font and colour still written directly; exit 1 while any is left
293	$RIPUL_THEME lint                           # the working tree's diff: did each replacement keep its value?
294	```
295	
296	`lint` knows the lines `migrate` writes. A line you added by hand in the same
297	diff (the root line, a list modifier) it reports as "the hunk adds and removes
298	different numbers of lines": that is the lint not knowing the line, not a
299	moved value.
300	
301	### What it leaves for you
302	
303	These need a person, because each is a decision or something the SDK does not
304	yet do for you.
305	
306	1. **Text with no colour of its own.** A `Text` that never had a colour is
307	   drawn in the system's label colour, not the theme's `text`. Give it
308	   `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.text))`. It must go on the text itself. On the
309	   root, or on a container, it changes what `.secondary` draws and recolours
310	   the labels of bordered and prominent buttons, links in a list and section
311	   headers, even under the default document (measured). Until the SDK finds
312	   a way, this is one line a text, and a new `Text` without it stays the
313	   system's colour silently.
314	2. **Lists.** A grouped list's ground, rows and separators stay the system's
315	   under a theme. Set them where you want them themed:
316	   `.scrollContentBackground(.hidden)` and `.background(.ripul(.surfaceSunken))`
317	   on the list, `.listRowBackground(Color.ripul(.surface))` on a section or a
318	   row (on the list itself it does nothing), `.listRowSeparatorTint(Color.ripul(.separator))`.
319	   Compare a screenshot under the default document afterwards: these have not
320	   been measured as identical by the SDK.
321	3. **Section headers and empty states.** `Section("Title")` becomes
322	   `Section(themed: "Title")`, a custom header `RipulSectionHeader { … }`, and
323	   `ContentUnavailableView("T", systemImage: "i")` becomes
324	   `ContentUnavailableView(themed: "T", systemImage: "i")`. Without these a
325	   header loses its weight under a themed family. Not inside a menu, a picker
326	   or a toolbar. A header takes the family and keeps the system's colour.
327	4. **A white or a blue that meant something.** `--named` writes the system
328	   form for white. Where the white sits on an accent fill, write
329	   `.ripul(.onAccent)`. Where a blue was the app's own colour and not a
330	   notice, write `.ripul(accentOr: .info)`: the accent once a theme names one.
331	5. **A colour of your own that is not one of the fifteen roles.** There is no
332	   place for it in the document yet. Keep it in your code, and if it should
333	   give way to the theme, read `RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent)` where it is
334	   used: `RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent) ? myNavy : Color.ripul(.accent)`.
335	6. **Fonts the command could not place:** a fixed size on a view that is
336	   neither a `Text` nor an `Image`, a font held in a property
337	   (`var titleFont: Font { .caption }` becomes `.ripul(.caption)`), `.rounded`
338	   and `.serif` designs, a font helper of your own (`static func serif(…) ->
339	   Font`), and with `--named` a `.black.opacity(…)` inside a gradient or a
340	   shadow. `check` lists them.
341	7. **Colours that are data** (a category's colour, a chart's, a brand mark):
342	   mark the line `// theme-exempt: <reason>` and leave it.
343	
344	Never keep a token in a `static let`, a model or a cache: it would not follow
345	a change. Read the accessor where the value is used.
346	
347	### Keeping it themed
348	
349	Run `check` in your build, so a new direct font or colour fails it. As a Run
350	Script phase:
351	
352	```bash
353	"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" check "$SRCROOT/<your source folder>"
354	```
355	
356	An app part way through adds `--baseline "$SRCROOT/theme-baseline.json"`: the
357	first run writes today's counts there, later runs fail only when a count
358	rises, and `--baseline <file> --update` lowers it. A zero from `check` is not
359	proof: it reads lines, not types, and cannot see a bare `.orange` passed to an
360	unlabelled parameter.
361	
362	## 5. Light and dark
363	
364	Both come from the document: every palette entry that should differ is a
365	pair. A role left at its default follows the system in both. Look at every
366	screen in both; the pair for `onAccent` is the one most often wrong (white on
367	a pale dark-mode accent cannot be read).
368	
369	## 6. Switching while the app runs
370	
371	```swift
372	RipulTheme.select("brand-large")              // another document in the bundle; kept for later launches
373	RipulTheme.select(RipulTheme.systemThemeName) // the system look, kept as a choice
374	RipulTheme.select(nil)                        // forget the choice: back to the theme the root names
375	RipulTheme.selectedTheme                      // what is in use; read in a body, it follows a change
376	RipulTheme.bundledThemes                      // every theme document in the bundle, with its own name
377	
378	RipulThemePicker("Look")                      // a picker over all of the above, in one line
379	```
380	
381	Everything on screen repaints, with nothing written in your views.
382	`select` returns false and changes nothing when the document is missing or
383	refused.
384	
385	Two more ways in, for a developer and for tests, with no code:
386	
387	- **A launch argument:** `-ripul.theme.document <name>`, with `system` for the
388	  system look. It is the `UserDefaults` key the choice is kept under, and as
389	  an argument it lasts for that one launch: nothing is stored.
390	- **A link, in a Debug build only:** `<your app's scheme>://theme?name=<name>`,
391	  with `name=system` for the system look. The root handles it. A store build
392	  ignores it; pass a URL to `RipulTheme.handleThemeLink(_:)` yourself if you
393	  want it there.
394	
395	A build that must show one theme whatever was chosen before installs with
396	`RipulTheme.install(theme: "brand", keepsChoice: false)`.
397	
398	What does not repaint by itself: UIKit code that read a colour or a font once
399	(read it again on `Notification.Name.ripulThemeDidChange`), and anything
400	computed outside a view's body and kept.
401	
402	## 7. The View Explorer names your tokens
403	
404	In a Debug build, selecting an element in the Ripul View Explorer lists the
405	theme tokens that style it, each with its value and whether it comes from the
406	document. The explorer reads that from a map written at build time. Add one
407	Run Script build phase holding one line:
408	
409	```bash
410	"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" usage-map
411	```
412	
413	In an XcodeGen `project.yml`:
414	
415	```yaml
416	    postCompileScripts:
417	      - name: Theme usage map
418	        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
419	        script: '"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" usage-map'
420	```
421	
422	It reads Xcode's own settings. It does nothing outside a Debug build, reads
423	the Swift files under the project's folder and the SDK's own screens, and
424	writes `ripul-theme-usage.json` into the app. It never fails a build. The
425	target needs `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = NO`, as any script that reads
426	the source does.
427	
428	An element is known by its identifier: `.uiKitIdentifier("screen.element")` or
429	`.accessibilityIdentifier(…)`. **Your own identifier modifier is followed.** If
430	the app names controls through a wrapper,
431	
432	```swift
433	func identified(_ name: String) -> some View { uiKitIdentifier(name) }
434	```
435	
436	then `.identified("stay.cottage")` is read like the two it wraps. Nothing
437	declares it; the build log says which wrappers it followed.
438	
439	To ask it directly: `$RIPUL_THEME usage-map --roots <folder> --no-sdk --stats`,
440	and `--explain <identifier>` for one element.
441	
442	## 8. Check that nothing moved
443	
444	Before the first edit (so before step 1, though it is written here), take
445	screenshots of your screens in light and dark, and take the whole set twice:
446	on iOS 26 and later a glass control differs between two captures of one build,
447	and the second set shows you which screens do that. After the migration, with
448	no document or an empty one, or launched with `-ripul.theme.document system`,
449	take them again and compare them pixel for pixel. Apart from those screens
450	they should be the same. Where they are not, a
451	replacement was a judgement and not an identity: `lint` names most of those,
452	and the lists and text colours of step 4 are the usual rest.
453	
454	## What the system draws that a theme does not reach
455	
456	- **Reached, with no edit:** the accent on toolbar buttons, toggles, buttons,
457	  menus, progress bars, sliders, the selected tab and alert buttons; the text
458	  family on form rows, buttons, navigation titles (large and inline),
459	  segmented controls and tab bar labels.
460	- **Not reached:** the colour of a large navigation title and of a section
461	  header (the family is); alerts' text, menus, swipe action labels, a menu
462	  picker's value; a navigation title on Mac Catalyst.
463	- **Under a themed accent, things that had no colour take it:** toolbar
464	  buttons, a swipe action with no tint, a toggle's on colour.
465	- A document cannot ask for a font feature (lining figures, for one).
466	- On Mac Catalyst give every sized role a `catalystSize`, and a presented view
467	  needs a root inside it. See "Measured again, with Mac Catalyst" in
468	  [theming.md](theming.md).
469	
470	## Not built
471	
472	Each of these is a decision the SDK has not taken yet. Until it is, the cost
473	is yours, as described above.
474	
475	- **A theme layer on its own.** The theme is part of `RipulAgent`: an app that
476	  wants only the theme links the whole package, in Release too.
477	- **Your own roles in the document.** The fifteen are all there are.
478	- **Text colour without a line a text.**
479	- **Lists themed from the root.**
480	- **Editing a theme in the app.** A look is tried by loading a document.
481	- The widgets and other extensions of an app are not themed unless they link
482	  the package and install the theme themselves.
483	
484	## The API in one place
485	
486	```swift
487	.ripulThemeRoot(theme: "brand")          // the root of your own tree
488	.ripulThemeRoot()                        // any other root; reads Info.plist's RipulTheme
489	RipulTheme.install(theme:bundle:keepsChoice:)
490	RipulTheme.select(_:)   RipulTheme.selectedTheme   RipulTheme.bundledThemes
491	RipulTheme.handleThemeLink(_:)           RipulThemePicker(_:systemTitle:)
492	RipulTheme.adopt(documentData:)          // a document from anywhere else, such as your server
493	RipulTheme.resetToDefaults()
494	RipulTheme.color(.accent)   RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent)
495	
496	Font.ripul(.body)   Font.ripul(.title, weight: .bold, family: .display)   Font.ripul(size: 14)
497	Font.ripulIcon(.title2)   Font.ripulIcon(size: 18)
498	.ripul(.textSecondary)            // as a style: foregroundStyle, fill, background, tint
499	Color.ripul(.danger)              // where a Color is required
500	.ripul(system: .systemGray5)      // a system colour, never themed
501	.ripul(accentOr: .info)
502	UIColor.ripul(.canvas)   UIFont.ripul(.caption)
503	.ripulTextStyle(.eyebrow)   .ripulProminentButtonStyle()   .ripulGlassProminentButtonStyle()   Section(themed:)   ContentUnavailableView(themed:)
504	```
505

# A theme for your app

This page is for an app that links the RipulAgent package and wants its own
fonts and colours to come from a theme: one JSON document, light and dark,
switchable while the app runs. It starts from "add the package" and is in the
order to do the work. The full contract, with every measurement behind a rule
here, is [theming.md](theming.md); you should not need it to get through this
page.

What you write, in total: one line at the root, a theme document, your font
files, one line of build setup for the View Explorer, and whatever the
migration command leaves for a person to decide. Everything else is the SDK's.

Where a thing is not built, this page says so. The list is at the end.

**If an agent is doing the work,** give it the procedure first: what to measure
before the first edit, which level to start at, where to stop and ask, and how
to prove nothing moved. It is a skill file in this package,
`tools/skills/theme-an-app/SKILL.md`, and one command copies it to where a
coding agent in your repository finds it (`.claude/skills` for Claude Code,
`.agents/skills` for Codex):

```bash
<the package checkout>/tools/ripul-theme install-skill <your repository>
```

An agent running inside Ripul reads the same text as the `theming` guide of its
`ripul_guide` tool. This page is the reference that procedure points to.

## The idea

Every token has a default that is the system value you write today.
`Font.ripul(.body)` is `Font.body`. `.ripul(.textSecondary)` is the system's
`.secondary` style. So moving a call site to a token changes no pixel, and an
app with no theme document looks exactly as it did. A document changes a token
only by naming it.

## With no change to your source

There are two ways to adopt the theme. The numbered steps below are the first:
you move your call sites to tokens, with a command that does most of it. This
section is the second: you change settings and add files, and no line of your
Swift changes. It is in the package from release 0.7.172, and it has been
measured on one app. It is where to start: the numbered steps are for an app
that wants what this does not reach.

What you do:

1. Add the package to the app target, as in step 1 below, without the root
   line.
2. Put your theme document and font files in the bundle (steps 2 and 3).
3. Switch on the package's build-tool plug-in, `RipulThemeRedirect`, for the app
   target: in Xcode, the target's Build Phases, "Run Build Tool Plug-ins", add
   it. In an XcodeGen `project.yml`:

   ```yaml
       buildToolPlugins:
         - plugin: RipulThemeRedirect
           package: RipulAgent
   ```
4. Allow the plug-in to run. Xcode asks once, "Trust & Enable". A command-line
   build passes `-skipPackagePluginValidation` to `xcodebuild`; without it the
   build fails with the one line `Validate plug-in “RipulThemeRedirect” in
   package “ripul-ios-sdk”` (measured with the package fetched by version; a
   package added by local path needs neither). Add the flag to your build
   scripts too.

With one theme document in the bundle, that document is the app's theme. With
several, name one with the Info.plist key `RipulTheme`.

**How it works.** On every build the plug-in writes one Swift file into the
build folder, and Xcode compiles it into your app's own module. The file
declares SwiftUI's names again: `Font.body` and the other text styles,
`Font.system(size:)`, `Color.red`, `Color(.systemBackground)`,
`.foregroundStyle(.secondary)`, `WindowGroup`. Inside your module your
declaration of a name is chosen over SwiftUI's, so your existing `.font(.body)`
calls the generated one, which is one call into the SDK. With no theme each
returns exactly what SwiftUI's would have. Nothing is added to your repository.

**What it reaches,** with no edit:

| You wrote | It follows |
|---|---|
| `.font(.body)`, `.font(.caption.weight(.semibold))`, `Font.body` | the type role of that name |
| `.font(.system(size: 14, weight: .medium))` | the text family at that size |
| `.system(.title, design: .serif)`, `.system(size: 22, design: .serif)`, and your own helper built on them | the display family, once a theme names one; the system's serif until then, with no second document |
| `design: .monospaced` | the code family |
| a font on an `Image` | nothing: a symbol keeps its system size |
| `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` and the other hierarchy styles | the text roles |
| `Color(.systemBackground)`, `Color(.systemGroupedBackground)`, `Color(.secondarySystemGroupedBackground)` | `canvas`, `surfaceSunken`, `surface` |
| `Color.red`, `.foregroundStyle(.orange)`, green, blue, gray | `danger`, `warning`, `success`, `info`, `neutral` |
| `WindowGroup { … }` | the theme root, with no line written: the accent, the body font for text with none, navigation titles, tab bar labels |
| identified elements | the View Explorer names their tokens (Debug builds), with no build phase |

**What it does not reach.** These stay the system's under a theme, where the
migration command or a line of yours would have reached them:

- text with no colour of its own, as in "What it leaves for you", 1;
- lists, section headers and empty states, as in 2 and 3;
- a prominent button's label (`onAccent`);
- a hierarchy style given to `fill`, `stroke` or `background`, and one passed
  through a variable of a generic type;
- a colour of your own (`Color("BrandNavy")`), and white and black;
- UIKit code (`UIFont.preferredFont`, `UIColor.label`);
- a `Label`'s icon, which takes its size from the label's font as before.

**What can go wrong.**

- A name you already declare (`extension Font { static var caption }`, a type
  called `WindowGroup`) is left out of the generated file and yours is used.
  The generator reads text, not types; one it misses is a compile error naming
  both places.
- A target is redirected only if the plug-in is on for it. A framework of your
  own needs it switched on too.
- `WindowGroup(for:)` and a UIKit app delegate are not covered: put
  `.ripulThemeRoot()` on the root yourself and add `RIPUL_THEME_NO_ROOT` to the
  target's Swift compilation conditions. `RIPUL_THEME_NO_STYLES` leaves
  `foregroundStyle` alone.
- A font or colour kept in a `static let` is read once and does not follow a
  switch while the app runs.
- The rule this rests on, that a module's own declaration is preferred to an
  imported one of the same name and type, is how the Swift compiler behaves
  (measured with Swift 6.4, Xcode 27.1, in Swift 5 and Swift 6 language
  modes). The language's documentation does not promise it.

The two ways mix: a file you have migrated calls the accessors directly, and
the rest goes through the generated file.

## 1. Add the package and name your theme

Pin the package (`https://github.com/ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk`), then put one
modifier on the root view of each window group:

```swift
import RipulAgent

WindowGroup {
    ContentView()
        .ripulThemeRoot(theme: "brand")     // brand.json in the app's bundle
}
```

That line is the whole setup. From it the SDK:

- finds `brand.json` in the bundle (at its top level, or in a folder named
  `Themes` or `Theme`), reads it and puts it in use before the first view is
  drawn;
- registers the font files the document names (step 3);
- keeps a choice made with `RipulTheme.select` between launches (step 6);
- falls back to `brand`, and then to the system look, when a document is
  missing, is not a theme document, or was written for a newer SDK. It logs
  which, with the prefix `[RipulTheme]`.

Two other ways to say the same thing, for an app that cannot put it on a root:

- the Info.plist key `RipulTheme` with the document's name, and a plain
  `.ripulThemeRoot()`;
- `RipulTheme.install(theme: "brand")` in the `App`'s `init` or the app
  delegate, for a UIKit app.

With no name at all, `.ripulThemeRoot()` leaves the app on the system look.

The root carries the accent (as the window's tint, so `.tint`,
`Color.accentColor` and control tints follow with no edit) and the theme's
body font for text with no font of its own. A sheet presented with
`.ripulSheet` has a root already. A presented `UIHostingController` of your
own needs `.ripulThemeRoot()` on its root view.

## 2. Write the document

Every key is optional, and an absent key is today's look. Start with
`{ "schema": 1, "name": "Brand" }`, which changes nothing, and add to it.

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "name": "Brand",
  "palette": {
    "navy":  { "light": "#24386b", "dark": "#a9bdeb" },
    "paper": { "light": "#f7f3ec", "dark": "#0d1428" },
    "ink":   "#1c2540"
  },
  "roles": {
    "ripul.accent": "navy",
    "ripul.canvas": "paper",
    "ripul.text": "ink"
  },
  "typography": {
    "families": { "text": "Source Sans 3", "display": "Playfair Display", "code": "system-monospaced" },
    "roles": {
      "display": { "size": 34, "weight": "bold" },
      "eyebrow": { "tracking": 1.8, "uppercase": true }
    }
  }
}
```

- **`palette`** names your colours. A value is `#RRGGBB`, `#RRGGBBAA`,
  `system:<name>` (a live system colour such as `system:label`), or a light
  and dark pair of those. Light and dark are written here and nowhere else.
- **`roles`** gives each colour role a palette name, another role, or a colour
  string. The fifteen roles, each with the system colour it is by default:

  | Role | Default | For |
  |---|---|---|
  | `accent` | the app's tint | selection, links, primary buttons |
  | `onAccent` | white | text and icons on an accent fill |
  | `canvas` | `systemBackground` | the app's background |
  | `surface` | `secondarySystemGroupedBackground` | cards and grouped rows |
  | `surfaceSunken` | `systemGroupedBackground` | the ground behind cards |
  | `text`, `textSecondary`, `textTertiary`, `textQuaternary` | `.primary` to `.quaternary` | text |
  | `separator` | `separator` | hairlines |
  | `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `neutral` | green, orange, red, blue, grey | state |

  The set is closed: a document cannot add a role (see the end).
- **`typography.families`** names the three families, `text`, `display` and
  `code`. Each is a font family you bundle, or one of `system`,
  `system-serif`, `system-rounded`, `system-monospaced`.
- **`typography.roles`** changes a type role: `size`, `weight`, `family`,
  `relativeTo`, `tracking`, `uppercase`, `catalystSize`. The roles are the
  eleven system text styles by their own names, plus `display` (a title in
  the display family), `eyebrow` and `code`.

**A serif that is yours already.** `"display": "system-serif"` draws what
`.font(.system(.title, design: .serif))` draws (compared pixel for pixel in a
host's trial on iOS 27, at the default text size). There is no accessor for
`design: .serif` itself. So an app whose headings are serif today keeps them
by naming `system-serif` as its display family and writing
`.font(.ripul(.title, family: .display))` at those headings. Its document is
then not empty, and the plain system look (`RipulTheme.systemThemeName`) is
not the look it had.

Check a dark value against its background yourself: nothing checks contrast.

## 3. Fonts

Put the font files in the app's bundle, at its top level or in a folder named
`Fonts`. Do nothing else. When a document names a family that is not the
system's, the SDK reads the bundled `.ttf`, `.otf` and `.ttc` files and
registers those that hold a face of that family. No `UIAppFonts` entry and no
registration call.

- The name in the document is the font's family name ("Source Sans 3"), not
  its file name.
- A variable font takes weights; a family with one weight draws that weight
  whatever is asked, and the system does not fake a bold.
- Ship each font's licence beside it. That is yours to get right.

## 4. Move the call sites: one command

The package brings its tools. In an Xcode project they are in the package
checkout, under the build's DerivedData:

```bash
# with -derivedDataPath build
RIPUL_THEME=build/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme
# with Xcode's default DerivedData
RIPUL_THEME=$(ls -d ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/<Project>-*/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme | head -1)
# in a Swift package
RIPUL_THEME=.build/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme
```

They need `python3` and nothing else.

```bash
$RIPUL_THEME migrate --dry-run --named <your source folder>   # what would change
$RIPUL_THEME migrate --named <your source folder>             # change it
```

Every rewrite is to the token whose default is the value it replaces, so
nothing moves on screen. It adds no import: each file it rewrote needs
`import RipulAgent`, or the app one `@_exported import RipulAgent`. It rewrites:

| You wrote | It writes |
|---|---|
| `.font(.body)`, `.font(.caption.weight(.semibold))` | `.font(.ripul(.body))`, `.font(.ripul(.caption, weight: .semibold))` |
| `.font(.title2)` or `.font(.system(size: 18))` on an `Image` | `.font(.ripulIcon(.title2))`, `.font(.ripulIcon(size: 18))`: a symbol's size, never themed |
| `.font(.system(size: 14, weight: .medium))` on a `Text` | `.font(.ripul(size: 14, weight: .medium))` |
| `.caption.monospaced()`, `design: .monospaced` | `family: .code` |
| `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` and the other hierarchy styles | `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))` |
| `Color.primary`, `Color.secondary` | `Color.ripul(.text)`, `Color.ripul(.textSecondary)` |
| `Color(.systemBackground)`, `UIColor.systemBackground`, `UIColor.label` | `Color.ripul(.canvas)`, `UIColor.ripul(.canvas)`, `UIColor.ripul(.text)` |
| any other system colour, `Color(.systemGray5)` | the system form, `Color.ripul(system: .systemGray5)`: drawn as before, never themed |
| `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)` | `.ripulProminentButtonStyle()`: its label is drawn in `onAccent` under a theme |
| `.buttonStyle(.glassProminent)` | `.ripulGlassProminentButtonStyle()`, likewise |
| with `--named`: `Color.red`, `.foregroundStyle(.orange)` | `Color.ripul(.danger)`, `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.warning))` |
| with `--named`: `.white`, `.black`, `.yellow` and the other hues | the system form, `.ripul(system: .white)` |

Then see what is left, and check the change:

```bash
$RIPUL_THEME check <your source folder>     # every font and colour still written directly; exit 1 while any is left
$RIPUL_THEME lint                           # the working tree's diff: did each replacement keep its value?
```

`lint` knows the lines `migrate` writes. A line you added by hand in the same
diff (the root line, a list modifier) it reports as "the hunk adds and removes
different numbers of lines": that is the lint not knowing the line, not a
moved value.

### What it leaves for you

These need a person, because each is a decision or something the SDK does not
yet do for you.

1. **Text with no colour of its own.** A `Text` that never had a colour is
   drawn in the system's label colour, not the theme's `text`. Give it
   `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.text))`. It must go on the text itself. On the
   root, or on a container, it changes what `.secondary` draws and recolours
   the labels of bordered and prominent buttons, links in a list and section
   headers, even under the default document (measured). Until the SDK finds
   a way, this is one line a text, and a new `Text` without it stays the
   system's colour silently.
2. **Lists.** A grouped list's ground, rows and separators stay the system's
   under a theme. Set them where you want them themed:
   `.scrollContentBackground(.hidden)` and `.background(.ripul(.surfaceSunken))`
   on the list, `.listRowBackground(Color.ripul(.surface))` on a section or a
   row (on the list itself it does nothing), `.listRowSeparatorTint(Color.ripul(.separator))`.
   Compare a screenshot under the default document afterwards: these have not
   been measured as identical by the SDK.
3. **Section headers and empty states.** `Section("Title")` becomes
   `Section(themed: "Title")`, a custom header `RipulSectionHeader { … }`, and
   `ContentUnavailableView("T", systemImage: "i")` becomes
   `ContentUnavailableView(themed: "T", systemImage: "i")`. Without these a
   header loses its weight under a themed family. Not inside a menu, a picker
   or a toolbar. A header takes the family and keeps the system's colour.
4. **A white or a blue that meant something.** `--named` writes the system
   form for white. Where the white sits on an accent fill, write
   `.ripul(.onAccent)`. Where a blue was the app's own colour and not a
   notice, write `.ripul(accentOr: .info)`: the accent once a theme names one.
5. **A colour of your own that is not one of the fifteen roles.** There is no
   place for it in the document yet. Keep it in your code, and if it should
   give way to the theme, read `RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent)` where it is
   used: `RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent) ? myNavy : Color.ripul(.accent)`.
6. **Fonts the command could not place:** a fixed size on a view that is
   neither a `Text` nor an `Image`, a font held in a property
   (`var titleFont: Font { .caption }` becomes `.ripul(.caption)`), `.rounded`
   and `.serif` designs, a font helper of your own (`static func serif(…) ->
   Font`), and with `--named` a `.black.opacity(…)` inside a gradient or a
   shadow. `check` lists them.
7. **Colours that are data** (a category's colour, a chart's, a brand mark):
   mark the line `// theme-exempt: <reason>` and leave it.

Never keep a token in a `static let`, a model or a cache: it would not follow
a change. Read the accessor where the value is used.

### Keeping it themed

Run `check` in your build, so a new direct font or colour fails it. As a Run
Script phase:

```bash
"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" check "$SRCROOT/<your source folder>"
```

An app part way through adds `--baseline "$SRCROOT/theme-baseline.json"`: the
first run writes today's counts there, later runs fail only when a count
rises, and `--baseline <file> --update` lowers it. A zero from `check` is not
proof: it reads lines, not types, and cannot see a bare `.orange` passed to an
unlabelled parameter.

## 5. Light and dark

Both come from the document: every palette entry that should differ is a
pair. A role left at its default follows the system in both. Look at every
screen in both; the pair for `onAccent` is the one most often wrong (white on
a pale dark-mode accent cannot be read).

## 6. Switching while the app runs

```swift
RipulTheme.select("brand-large")              // another document in the bundle; kept for later launches
RipulTheme.select(RipulTheme.systemThemeName) // the system look, kept as a choice
RipulTheme.select(nil)                        // forget the choice: back to the theme the root names
RipulTheme.selectedTheme                      // what is in use; read in a body, it follows a change
RipulTheme.bundledThemes                      // every theme document in the bundle, with its own name

RipulThemePicker("Look")                      // a picker over all of the above, in one line
```

Everything on screen repaints, with nothing written in your views.
`select` returns false and changes nothing when the document is missing or
refused.

Two more ways in, for a developer and for tests, with no code:

- **A launch argument:** `-ripul.theme.document <name>`, with `system` for the
  system look. It is the `UserDefaults` key the choice is kept under, and as
  an argument it lasts for that one launch: nothing is stored.
- **A link, in a Debug build only:** `<your app's scheme>://theme?name=<name>`,
  with `name=system` for the system look. The root handles it. A store build
  ignores it; pass a URL to `RipulTheme.handleThemeLink(_:)` yourself if you
  want it there.

A build that must show one theme whatever was chosen before installs with
`RipulTheme.install(theme: "brand", keepsChoice: false)`.

What does not repaint by itself: UIKit code that read a colour or a font once
(read it again on `Notification.Name.ripulThemeDidChange`), and anything
computed outside a view's body and kept.

## 7. The View Explorer names your tokens

In a Debug build, selecting an element in the Ripul View Explorer lists the
theme tokens that style it, each with its value and whether it comes from the
document. The explorer reads that from a map written at build time. Add one
Run Script build phase holding one line:

```bash
"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" usage-map
```

In an XcodeGen `project.yml`:

```yaml
    postCompileScripts:
      - name: Theme usage map
        basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false
        script: '"${BUILD_DIR%/Build/*}/SourcePackages/checkouts/ripul-ios-sdk/tools/ripul-theme" usage-map'
```

It reads Xcode's own settings. It does nothing outside a Debug build, reads
the Swift files under the project's folder and the SDK's own screens, and
writes `ripul-theme-usage.json` into the app. It never fails a build. The
target needs `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = NO`, as any script that reads
the source does.

An element is known by its identifier: `.uiKitIdentifier("screen.element")` or
`.accessibilityIdentifier(…)`. **Your own identifier modifier is followed.** If
the app names controls through a wrapper,

```swift
func identified(_ name: String) -> some View { uiKitIdentifier(name) }
```

then `.identified("stay.cottage")` is read like the two it wraps. Nothing
declares it; the build log says which wrappers it followed.

To ask it directly: `$RIPUL_THEME usage-map --roots <folder> --no-sdk --stats`,
and `--explain <identifier>` for one element.

## 8. Check that nothing moved

Before the first edit (so before step 1, though it is written here), take
screenshots of your screens in light and dark, and take the whole set twice:
on iOS 26 and later a glass control differs between two captures of one build,
and the second set shows you which screens do that. After the migration, with
no document or an empty one, or launched with `-ripul.theme.document system`,
take them again and compare them pixel for pixel. Apart from those screens
they should be the same. Where they are not, a
replacement was a judgement and not an identity: `lint` names most of those,
and the lists and text colours of step 4 are the usual rest.

## What the system draws that a theme does not reach

- **Reached, with no edit:** the accent on toolbar buttons, toggles, buttons,
  menus, progress bars, sliders, the selected tab and alert buttons; the text
  family on form rows, buttons, navigation titles (large and inline),
  segmented controls and tab bar labels.
- **Not reached:** the colour of a large navigation title and of a section
  header (the family is); alerts' text, menus, swipe action labels, a menu
  picker's value; a navigation title on Mac Catalyst.
- **Under a themed accent, things that had no colour take it:** toolbar
  buttons, a swipe action with no tint, a toggle's on colour.
- A document cannot ask for a font feature (lining figures, for one).
- On Mac Catalyst give every sized role a `catalystSize`, and a presented view
  needs a root inside it. See "Measured again, with Mac Catalyst" in
  [theming.md](theming.md).

## Not built

Each of these is a decision the SDK has not taken yet. Until it is, the cost
is yours, as described above.

- **A theme layer on its own.** The theme is part of `RipulAgent`: an app that
  wants only the theme links the whole package, in Release too.
- **Your own roles in the document.** The fifteen are all there are.
- **Text colour without a line a text.**
- **Lists themed from the root.**
- **Editing a theme in the app.** A look is tried by loading a document.
- The widgets and other extensions of an app are not themed unless they link
  the package and install the theme themselves.

## The API in one place

```swift
.ripulThemeRoot(theme: "brand")          // the root of your own tree
.ripulThemeRoot()                        // any other root; reads Info.plist's RipulTheme
RipulTheme.install(theme:bundle:keepsChoice:)
RipulTheme.select(_:)   RipulTheme.selectedTheme   RipulTheme.bundledThemes
RipulTheme.handleThemeLink(_:)           RipulThemePicker(_:systemTitle:)
RipulTheme.adopt(documentData:)          // a document from anywhere else, such as your server
RipulTheme.resetToDefaults()
RipulTheme.color(.accent)   RipulTheme.isDefault(.accent)

Font.ripul(.body)   Font.ripul(.title, weight: .bold, family: .display)   Font.ripul(size: 14)
Font.ripulIcon(.title2)   Font.ripulIcon(size: 18)
.ripul(.textSecondary)            // as a style: foregroundStyle, fill, background, tint
Color.ripul(.danger)              // where a Color is required
.ripul(system: .systemGray5)      // a system colour, never themed
.ripul(accentOr: .info)
UIColor.ripul(.canvas)   UIFont.ripul(.caption)
.ripulTextStyle(.eyebrow)   .ripulProminentButtonStyle()   .ripulGlassProminentButtonStyle()   Section(themed:)   ContentUnavailableView(themed:)
```

353	    static func parse(_ data: Data) throws -> (table: Table, part: Data?) {
354	        guard let document = (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data)) as? [String: Any] else {
355	            throw DocumentError.notAnObject
356	        }
357	        let part = document[reservedKey] as? [String: Any] ?? document
358	        if let schema = (part["schema"] as? NSNumber)?.intValue, schema > RipulTheme.schema {
359	            throw DocumentError.newerSchema(schema)
360	        }
361	        var palette: [String: RipulColorValue] = [:]
362	        for (name, raw) in part["palette"] as? [String: Any] ?? [:] {
363	            if let value = colorValue(fromJSON: raw) { palette[name] = value }
364	        }

367	            guard let reference = raw as? String else { continue }
368	            references[name.hasPrefix(prefix) ? String(name.dropFirst(prefix.count)) : name] = reference

input.description: Measure no-edit text and list theming
input.prompt:
You are running a measurement, not writing a feature. Work only under /tmp/theme-probe (create it). Do not edit, commit or stash anything in /Users/petermaude/Documents/ripul or any other repository. Report measured facts; mark anything reasoned as reasoned.

BACKGROUND
An iOS SDK themes a host SwiftUI app from one JSON document. Two things are not reached today without the host editing its source, and I need to know whether the SDK can carry them from the outside (from a root modifier, from UIKit, or from process-level hooks installed by the SDK), with NO change to the host's views:
 (A) A SwiftUI `Text` with no colour of its own stays the system's black/white (label colour) when the theme names a text colour. Already measured twice and NOT to be repeated: `.foregroundStyle(x)` on the root or on a container changes what `.secondary` draws and recolours the labels of bordered and prominent buttons, links in a list and section headers.
 (B) A grouped `List`/`Form`: its ground, its rows' background, its separators and its section header colour stay the system's.

Hard requirement for any mechanism: when the theme names nothing, the mechanism must not be installed at all, so the app is the system's own, pixel for pixel. So you only need to measure the "theme names a colour" state for function, plus confirm the mechanism can be removed/uninstalled at run time (theme switched back to system while running).

WHAT TO BUILD
A scratch SwiftUI app (iOS 17 deployment target, Swift, built with /Applications/Xcode-27.1.app via xcodebuild, DerivedData under /tmp/theme-probe/dd; generate the project with xcodegen, which is installed). One screen in a TabView/NavigationStack with a large title and a toolbar button, containing every container below, each element with distinct text:
 - bare `Text("plain")`, `Text("secondary").foregroundStyle(.secondary)`, tertiary too, a `Text` with `.foregroundStyle(.white)` on a coloured fill, a `Label("label", systemImage:)`
 - `Button("plain button")`, `.buttonStyle(.bordered)`, `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)`, a `Button { } label: { Text("custom label") }` bordered, a `Link`
 - a second screen pushed or in a second tab: `List` with `.insetGrouped` default style holding `Section("Header") { Text row, NavigationLink row, Button row, Toggle row, a LabeledContent row } footer`, and a `Form` with a TextField and a Picker
 - a toolbar item with text, a `Menu`, and a way to present an `.alert` and a `.sheet` containing bare Text (drive them with launch arguments so no tapping is needed: e.g. `-probe.screen list`, `-probe.alert 1`, `-probe.mechanism <name>`, `-probe.themed 1`).
Launch arguments choose the screen and the mechanism so each state can be screenshotted with `xcrun simctl io <udid> screenshot` in light and dark (`xcrun simctl ui <udid> appearance dark`).

Borrow a simulator, do not just pick one (other agents use them): `ripul-train acquire simulators os=27 type=iPhone --reason "theme probe: text and list measurement" --wait` prints which simulator is yours; `ripul-train release <lease>` when finished (always release). If `ripul-train` is not on PATH look in /Users/petermaude/Documents/ripul/ripul-native-app/macOS/trainyard/ for it and its README.

Use obviously visible test colours: text = a strong magenta-ish ink in light and a yellow in dark; secondary = green; list ground = pale orange / dark purple; rows = pale blue / dark teal; separator = red.

MECHANISMS TO MEASURE (each alone, then the promising ones together)
 M1. Method swizzling of UIKit's public system colour class getters: `+[UIColor labelColor]`, `secondaryLabelColor`, `tertiaryLabelColor`, `quaternaryLabelColor`, `systemGroupedBackgroundColor`, `secondarySystemGroupedBackgroundColor`, `separatorColor`, `systemBackgroundColor` (exchange implementations with ones returning dynamic test colours; keep the originals callable). Question 1: does a bare SwiftUI `Text` follow `labelColor`? Does `.secondary` follow `secondaryLabelColor`? Question 2: does a grouped List's ground, row background, separator, header text follow? Question 3: what ELSE changes (button labels, links, toolbar, nav title, alert text, menu, text field text and placeholder, tab bar)? Swizzle before the first window exists (App.init) and also try swizzling late (after first frame) to see whether UIKit/SwiftUI cached the colours.
 M2. UIKit appearance proxies and direct UIKit configuration, public API only: `UICollectionView.appearance().backgroundColor`, `UITableView.appearance()...`, `UICollectionViewListCell.appearance()` / `UITableViewCell.appearance().backgroundColor`, `UITableViewHeaderFooterView`/`UILabel.appearance(whenContainedInInstancesOf:)` for header text colour, `UICollectionView.appearance().separatorColor` if any. Which parts of a SwiftUI List on iOS 27 do they reach?
 M3. From the root only (a modifier applied once around the whole app content): `.scrollContentBackground(.hidden)` at the root plus a background — does it reach Lists below it, and is the app's ground then visible behind the list? `.listRowBackground(...)`, `.listRowSeparatorTint(...)`, `.listSectionSeparatorTint` applied at the root (expected not to work: confirm). `.backgroundStyle(...)` at the root. Any environment value settable at the root that a list row's background reads.
 M4. Walking the window's UIKit view hierarchy from a hidden probe view (the SDK already does this for tab bar labels): find the `UICollectionView` backing each List, set its `backgroundColor`; for each visible `UICollectionViewListCell` set `backgroundConfiguration` (or `configurationUpdateHandler`) to the test row colour; set separator colour through the list layout configuration if reachable with public API. Do the values survive scrolling, cell reuse, a SwiftUI state update that re-renders the list, selection highlight, and presenting a new screen (needs re-walk: say what trigger would be needed)? 
 M5. Anything else you can find that uses only public API and needs nothing written in the host's views (for instance a custom UITraitCollection-based route, `UIColor` asset overrides, an `EnvironmentValues` key). Do NOT use private selectors, underscore-prefixed SwiftUI API, or `dlsym`: this ships to the App Store.

For the swizzle, also measure the cost of removing it at run time (exchange back) and whether already-drawn views repaint after a `setNeedsDisplay`/trait change or need something else.

HOW TO JUDGE
Open the screenshots yourself (Read tool on the PNG) and report, per mechanism and per element, one of: follows / does not follow / changed but should not have. Light and dark both. Note anything that looked broken (unreadable text, lost selection highlight, lost inset-card shape or corner radius, wrong header colour).

REPORT (your final message; it is read by an engineer, be exact and brief)
1. A table: rows = elements (bare text, secondary text, bordered button label, prominent button label, plain button label, Link, list ground, list row background, list row text, row separator, section header, section footer, nav large title, inline title, toolbar button, tab bar, alert text, menu, text field text, sheet text), columns = M1..M5, cells as above.
2. For text (A): is there a no-host-edit mechanism that themes bare text without recolouring controls? Which, and what are its side effects?
3. For lists (B): the smallest set of mechanisms that themes ground + rows + separators + header with no host edit, and what breaks.
4. The exact code of the winning mechanism(s) (paste the Swift), and the paths of the scratch project and the key screenshots.
5. What you did not measure.
Time box: about 45 minutes of work. If the simulator pool is all taken for more than 10 minutes, say so and stop.

    url: https://github.com/ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk
    exactVersion: 0.7.171

targets:
  SandsendRetreats:

    platform: iOS
    sources:

        INFOPLIST_KEY_UILaunchScreen_Generation: YES
        INFOPLIST_KEY_UIApplicationSceneManifest_Generation: YES
        INFOPLIST_KEY_UISupportedInterfaceOrientations_iPhone: UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait

        # The usage map's script reads the source.
